In 1648, accordingly the price of the best wheat at Windsor Market appears from the same
accounts to have been four fives, and in 1649 to have been four pounds the quarter
of nine bushels, the excess of those two years above two tens.
The average price of the sixteen years preceding 1637 is three fives, which, divided among
the sixty-four last years of the last century, will alone very nearly account for that small
enhancement of price which seems to have taken place in them.
These, however, though the highest, are by no means the only high prices which seem to
have been occasioned by the Civil Wars.
